definition: A condition caused by excess fluid in the lungs, making breathing difficult.
general_symptoms: Shortness of breath (dyspnea), especially during movement or lying down
Shortness of breath when lying flat
Feeling of breathlessness that awakens you
Gasping for air / feeling like you're suffocating
Coughing up of foam and loose mucus
Coughing up blood or frothy mucus
general_diagnosis_methods: Physical exam (listening to heart and lungs with a stethoscope)
Checking for increased or decreased heart rate or blood pressure
Checking for crackling sounds or wheezing/whistling sounds in lungs
Checking for gray or bluish skin
general_treatments: Oxygen delivered through prongs in your nose
Machines that blow air into your lungs through a mask on your face
Ventilators or respirators that blow in air through a tube inserted into your windpipe
Medications that cause you to urinate more and get rid of fluid
general_outlook: Can be life-threatening and requires immediate medical treatment
Survival rates depend on the cause of the condition and how quickly you receive treatment
Severe cases can be life-threatening if you don't receive treatment right away
prevention: Take medications as directed if you have a heart condition
See your healthcare provider regularly and if you have problems breathing
Eat a healthy diet low in salt
Talk to your provider if you're planning activities (such as mountain climbing) that can cause pulmonary edema

causes: Heart valves that are leaky or narrowed (valvular heart disease)

causes_by_etiology_and_subtypes.category_name: Noncardiogenic Causes (Inflammation or Injury to Blood Vessels in Lungs)

specific_subtypes.definition: A noncardiogenic form of pulmonary edema occurring at high elevations due to reduced oxygen pressure.
causes: Being at high altitudes or rapidly going up (ascending) a mountain
Lower oxygen levels at higher altitudes
Pulmonary blood vessels constricting and becoming leaky
outlook: Medical emergency and can be life-threatening

specific_subtypes.definition: A form of noncardiogenic pulmonary edema triggered by immersion in water during swimming or diving.
causes: Capillaries bursting during competitive swimming and diving
Blood sent to lungs from legs and abdomen during diving, increasing pressure in lung blood vessels and causing fluid to leak into air sacs
Bleeding or swelling in your brain
Blockage in upper airway and straining to breathe
